subject: ventures/ids-model-check
professional: a senior BIM information manager (ISO 19650) who writes and enforces IDS files for clients, with the eye of a buildingSMART IDS implementer; first checks: does it score buildingSMART's official IDS 1.0 test pairs, does it agree with the reference implementation (IfcOpenShell's IfcTester) on real models, are values converted to SI from the project's units as IDS requires (lengths, areas, temperatures), do type-object properties inherit with occurrence override, does the IFC2X3 type mapping resolve IfcFlowTerminal occurrences, and does the BCF it writes validate against buildingSMART's BCF 2.1 schemas

evidence.correctness: Fetched buildingSMART's IDS test cases at the pinned commit 870f9c4 into the scratchpad and scored them with my own 15-line runner (scratchpad/ids-model-check/mytc.mjs, expected verdict read from buildingSMART's file names): {"fail->fail":120,"invalid->invalid":26,"pass->pass":187,"invalid->fail":1}, i.e. 334 of 334 right, 26 of 27 invalid flagged, 0 of 307 valid files called invalid, exactly as claimed (the author's eval/run-testcases.mjs prints the same). Installed IfcTester 0.9.0.post1 / IfcOpenShell in a venv and compared status, applicable count and failing element ids spec by spec (scratchpad cmp.sh): 54 of 54 identical on the three committed buildingSMART IFC 4.3 models (Building-Hvac, Infra-Rail, Infra-Road) x infrastructure-and-mep.ids.xml; 13 of 14 on the tiny house x two starter IDS (the 14th is the README's documented multiple-xs:pattern case, where XSD ORs patterns and this checker is right; IfcTester also lists no failing ids for a prohibited spec, status agrees). Hand-built an IFC4 model in feet with a type-object Pset overridden on one occurrence, a material layer set usage, a Uniclass reference and nested spatial containment, wrote 7 specifications with verdicts derived by hand from IDS 1.0: all 7 as derived (W-A fails REI60 because its occurrence REI30 overrides the type; 10 ft = 3.048 m passes 3..5 m, 20 ft = 6.096 m fails) and 7 of 7 identical in IfcTester. A units model (inch defined on a MILLI METRE base, MILLI SQUARE_METRE areas, DEGREE_CELSIUS): 120 in = 3.048 m, 12,000,000 mm2 = 12 m2 and 26 C = 299.15 K all pass as hand-computed; IfcTester fails the Celsius case (it does not apply the 273.15 offset), so this checker is the more correct of the two there. BCF export of the sample (4 topics) validates against buildingSMART's BCF-XML release_2_1 markup.xsd, visinfo.xsd and version.xsd with xmllint. Real-model performance claims (22 MB Revit export in 1.4 s, 219 MB federated model) were not re-run: those models are not in the tree.
evidence.completeness: Every claim I could exercise worked end to end: STEP, ifcXML and .ifczip of the sample give the same 3 of 7 result; text, --json, --junit (well-formed, 7 testcases) and --bcf (schema-valid) outputs; --audit (VALID on my own IDS files, INVALID reasons on the 27 invalid suite files); ci-cli.mjs over 3 model/IDS pairs exits 1 on a required failure and treats optional failures as warnings; unreadable input exits 2 with 'not a STEP file: no DATA section' and a truncated file reports a reader note instead of passing. CSV export exists in report.mjs/index.html only (not in the CLI, which the README does not claim). The IDS editor (editor.html/editor.mjs, 1,300 lines) was covered only through its unit tests, not driven in a browser. No TODOs or stubs found in the engine; NEXT.md lists open items honestly (a real BIM coordinator's IDS and model needs a person).
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' (Node 22): 278 tests, 276 pass, 2 skipped, 2.9 s. The two skipped are the headline ones: 'buildingSMART's IDS test pairs all score right' and 'BCF export validates against buildingSMART's BCF 2.1 schemas', both skipped unless eval/fetch-testcases.sh and eval/fetch-bcf-schemas.sh were run, and ventures-tests.yml / run_venture_tests.py fetch neither, so CI never runs the 334-pair conformance check. Seeded 6 mutants with quality_mutate.py: float tolerance 1e-6 -> 1e-5 caught; type-overrides-occurrence pset merge caught; maxInclusive <= -> < caught; all three unit-conversion mutants SURVIVED both the unit suite and buildingSMART's 334 pairs: SQUARE_ prefix not squared (mm2 read as 1e-3), DEGREE_CELSIUS offset 273.15 -> 0, conversion-based unit ignoring its base unit's prefix. Only one unit test exists (engine.test.mjs:67, MILLI METRE length).
evidence.craft: Read ids.mjs (1,595 lines: unitScale 220-246, floatEq 256-261, restriction matching 370-405, psetSources/psetsOf 640-697), cli.mjs, the test files' unit sections. Engine is dependency-free ES modules with docstrings stating each IDS rule and why; errors surface (exit 2, reader notes) rather than silently passing. Defects: ids.mjs and editor.mjs are large single modules; README.md is 73 KB and llms.txt 28 KB of dated changelog paragraphs (single lines of several thousand characters), which buries the usage a reader needs; the long-lived eval scripts (149 files) are fine as evidence but the README duplicates their findings in prose.
evidence.claims: Checked 8 claims: 334/334 buildingSMART pairs (pass, recomputed); 26 of 27 invalid flagged, none of 307 valid (pass, recomputed; the 27th is partof/invalid-a_group_predefined_type_must_match_exactly_1_2, scored fail not invalid, as the page FAQ says); same answers as IfcTester except multiple xs:pattern (pass on the samples, observed exactly that case); IFC 4.3 Simple-Scene 348 of 348 (partial: 54 of 54 on the 3 models in the tree, the other 9 not fetched); BCF 2.1 export (pass, schema-valid); nothing uploaded (pass: page fetches only ./schema/*.json and, on 'try the sample', its own samples/); disclaimer present on index.html:131 and editor.html:88, usage counters via usage.mjs with opt-out. Not backed: llms.txt:42 'Not covered: ... validation of the IDS file against the IDS XML schema' contradicts the same file's and README's structure.mjs ids.xsd check (stale); README:804 says unit tests cover 'unit conversion' but only millimetre lengths are tested. served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin in llms.txt, sitemap, robots, canonicals.
evidence.fitness: Walked the BIM manager's job: drop a consultant model and the client's IDS, read each specification with the failing elements and the reason ('Pset_WallCommon.FireRating is "REI30", not "REI60"'), export BCF that a BIM tool can import (schema-valid, one topic per failing element selected by IfcGuid), and gate the same check in CI with JUnit and annotations. That is the real job and it completes, with no install or upload, which IfcTester and Solibri do not offer. The IDS audit and repair cover the common failure that client IDS files are themselves invalid. Gap: no real coordinator's project IDS and model have been run (NEXT.md says so), and the editor was not driven in a browser here.
evidence.domain: Against IDS 1.0 (buildingSMART's documentation and test suite) and IfcTester: facets, cardinality, IDS float tolerance (|x-v| <= 1e-6|v| + 1e-6), XSD pattern semantics (patterns ORed, anchors literal), occurrence-overrides-type property inheritance, IFC2X3 type mapping (IFCAIRTERMINAL finds an IfcFlowTerminal typed by IfcAirTerminalType; checked on a hand IFC2X3 model, same as IfcTester) and SI conversion including temperature offsets all follow the standard, and on two points (multiple patterns, Celsius) it is more faithful than the reference implementation. A senior reviewer would sign off on the method; what they would ask for is evidence on real project IDS files and a regression gate for the conformance suite and unit handling.

defects.what: Unit conversion to SI is untested beyond millimetre lengths: three seeded mutants (prefixed areas not squared, Celsius offset dropped, a conversion-based unit ignoring its base unit's prefix) pass all 276 unit tests and buildingSMART's 334 pairs. The code is right today (hand-checked: 12e6 mm2 = 12 m2, 26 C = 299.15 K, 120 in on a MILLI METRE base = 3.048 m), but a regression would silently flip area and temperature verdicts on real MEP and space models.

The headline conformance test (334 buildingSMART pairs) and the BCF 2.1 schema test are skipped unless the corpora are fetched by hand, and the ventures-tests workflow never fetches them, so CI has never gated the claim the page leads with; a change that broke a facet would merge green.

llms.txt's 'Not covered' list says 'validation of the IDS file against the IDS XML schema', contradicting the same file's Use section, the README and structure.mjs, which do check ids.xsd. An LLM reading llms.txt gets both answers.
README says the unit tests cover 'unit conversion'; one test covers millimetre lengths only (engine.test.mjs:67).
README.md (73 KB) and llms.txt (28 KB) are dated changelogs with multi-thousand-character lines; the usage a BIM manager needs is buried under per-session eval summaries.

verdict: The checker's answers are right and independently confirmed: my own runner scores buildingSMART's 334 IDS 1.0 test pairs 334 of 334 (26 of 27 invalid flagged, no valid file called invalid); IfcTester 0.9.0.post1 gives identical status, applicable counts and failing ids on 54 of 54 IFC 4.3 specifications and on hand-built feet and IFC2X3 models, differing only where this checker follows XSD (multiple patterns) or SI (Celsius to Kelvin) and IfcTester does not; hand-computed unit conversions (inch on a mm base, mm2, Celsius) pass; the BCF export validates against buildingSMART's BCF 2.1 schemas. It misses the bar on verification alone: the conformance suite and BCF schema tests skip in CI because nothing fetches their corpora, and three seeded unit-conversion mutants (areas, temperature offset, conversion-unit base prefix) survive both the 276 unit tests and the 334 pairs. Minor claim drift: llms.txt still lists ids.xsd validation as not covered, and the README overstates unit-conversion test coverage.
